language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hi, my name is Hanalel! Meet my friend Tim. Today we have come to visit the Alexendrian Lighthouse and the garden to have some fun.
Hey, there! Hanale, why don't you move the ball over here?
Sure! You know Tim, I wonder how this ball moves.
Hanale, it is force—a concept in science—that moves all objects.
Wow! That sounds interesting. Tim, can you tell me more?
Well, when we try to push or pull something, we apply force to the objects. Let's find out more by playing a few games.

Thank you for helping!
Tim do you have any idea why a ball always returns to the ground after it is thrown up in the air?
Yes! it's because of the gravitational force, which is a pull force by the earth. Gravitational force is a non-contact force, like magnetic or electrostatic force.
There are also contact forces. Those require two surfaces to be in touch. They are classified as: normal force, frictional force, tension force, and spring force.
Can you help me identify the different types of forces?

No…

There are multiple forces surrounding objects. To find out which way an object is moving at what speed, you need to find and compare all the different forces that surround the object. Don't forget to check the size of the object, that's also
